title: Briam
subtitle: Greek roast vegetable bake with olive oil and herbs
excerpt: Courgette, aubergine, potato and tomato layered in a roasting tin and baked slowly in olive oil until soft and golden at the edges. A Greek summer classic that needs no attention once it is in the oven.
sourceNotes: Greek ladera tradition, related to the French ratatouille. Common across mainland Greece and the islands.

recipe.batchNotes: Use a second roasting tin. Rotate the tins halfway through for even cooking.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Excellent made a few hours ahead and eaten at room temperature. Keeps for three days refrigerated.

content.text: Briam is a slow oven bake, not a stir-fry. The vegetables give up their moisture gradually and then start to caramelise at the edges. Do not rush this with high heat or they will dry out before they soften.
Heat the oven to 190C. Toss the sliced onion and garlic in a large roasting tin with half the olive oil, the oregano, salt and pepper.
Layer the potato, courgette, aubergine and tomato slices in overlapping rows on top of the onion. There is no set order; alternate as you like.
Drizzle the remaining olive oil over everything. Season with a little more salt.
Cover tightly with foil. Bake for 50 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake for a further 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden and the potatoes are tender when pierced with a knife.
Rest for 10 minutes out of the oven. Scatter over the parsley and serve.

items.cause: They were sliced too thick, or the oven was not hot enough.
items.fix: Cover again and bake for a further 15 to 20 minutes, checking every 5 minutes.

items.cause: Too much liquid released from the tomatoes and was not reduced.
items.fix: Pour off excess liquid and return the tin to the oven uncovered for 15 minutes.

items.symptom: The top is browning too fast.
items.cause: The foil was removed too early or the oven runs hot.
items.fix: Lay the foil back loosely on top and continue baking until the potatoes are done.
